answer: 00955630 is a single closed-form, drag-free parabola solve. It computes the world yaw first (atan2 of the floored-normalized delta) and writes it through argument 6 before touching the pitch. With R = sqrt(dx*dx + dz*dz), h = aim.y - muzzle.y, v = muzzleSpeed and the immediate g = 9.81 at 00CF9058, it forms k = g*R*R/(2*v*v) (009556AE..009556C4) and D = R*R - 4*k*(k + h) (009556C8..009556EE, the 4.0 is the double at 00D7A328). FCOMIP/JBE at 009556F8 takes the success path on 0.0 <= D, so a NaN discriminant also solves. On success FSUBR at 00955728 picks the MINUS root, tan(pitch) = (R - sqrt(D)) / (2*k) - the low flat trajectory; the high root is unreachable in this build. On D < 0 the pitch is the float pi/4 at 00CEB5A8 and AL is 0, but the common tail still runs, so both outputs are always valid wrapped angles. The tail rebuilds a world direction from the pair (004B4D80), and only when ECX is non-NULL transforms it into the mount's cached affine inverse at mount+110h (0042D0D0, normalize = 0) and re-extracts the pair (00521370). The yaw is then negated against the float -0.0f at 00D7A208 and both angles wrapped into (-pi, pi] by 00605070 - unconditionally, world-frame case included. There is no drag, no air density, no time of flight, no iteration and no per-weapon or per-world gravity input.

routines.abi_evidence: The argument count is the RET immediate, not the pushes: 0095581F RET 0x10 pops four stack dwords. The frame balances exactly - SUB ESP,0x20 plus PUSH EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI (0x30) against POP EDI/ESI/EBP/EBX plus ADD ESP,0x20 (0x30) - so [ESP+34h/38h/3Ch/40h] are those four arguments for the body. ECX is read into ESI at 00955646 and EDX is dereferenced at 00955637 before either is written, which makes it __fastcall with six parameters.

assumptions: 00B63D50 really computes the affine inverse of mount+0CCh. Its entry convention and its exit stores were read; its 145-instruction interior was not, and the existing ledger name is taken on trust. If it is not a true inverse, every mount-local pair this routine returns is wrong by whatever it actually computes - follow-up 3.

mount+110h is a similarity transform, so a unit world direction stays unit through 0042D0D0 (called with normalize = 0) and 00521370 only clamps y. A mount matrix with non-uniform scale would distort the recovered pitch; no such mount was looked for.

The parameter names mount, aimPoint, muzzlePos, muzzleSpeed, outPitch, outYaw describe how the six call sites use the slots. They are not recovered identifiers, and neither is BSP_Gun_SolveGravityArc.

The reconstruction preserves the x87 evaluation order and the float round trips of k, k + h, D, sqrt(D) and the tangent, but not the 53-bit x87 intermediate precision: Win32 MSVC evaluates double expressions at 64 bits. This is a bounded implementation - reconstructed and build-tested, not ABI-compatible and not game-validated.
